correctness.rationale: The normalized adjacency has explicitly normalized cosine eigenvectors and pairwise distinct spectral nodes. The determinant of each r-time observation matrix factors as a nonzero temporal Vandermonde times the product of its sensor eigenvector values. This yields the exact j-dependent Gram ratio. For three modes, the secondary \(|\cos\theta\cos2\theta|\) lobe has maximum \(2/(3\sqrt6)\), below the value \(\sqrt3/4\) at \(\theta=\pi/6\), and direct \(2\le n\le5\) boundary calculation gives endpoint optimality. For all r, a rigorous cosine-product lower bound plus monotonicity gives unique \(j=1,n-1\) for \(n\ge4(r-1)^3\). CHECK.py reproduces numerical eigenvector, matrix-determinant, sharp-three-mode, and sufficient-bound cases; finite checks do not replace the quantified proof.

value.rationale: Single-node sensor placement for bandlimited graph Paley-Wiener dynamical frames is a motivated D-optimal design question. The sharp seven-vertex transition contradicts extrapolation of full-band endpoint optimality to three low modes, and a uniform all-fixed-band eventual optimality law works for any injective spectral evolution. The exact determinant objective has standard information-volume meaning; conclusions are not made about a different conditioning criterion.
